title: Inventory: fix a bug, add two operations and an error variant
steps: Bug: total_value must return the sum of qty * price over all items.
low_stock must return its skus sorted ascending.

Add remove_stock(inv, sku, n), with n > 0, that decreases that item's qty by n and keeps the list order. Raise UnknownSku(sku) if no item has that sku, and OutOfStock(sku, wanted=n, have=<current qty>) if n is larger than the qty.
Add an error variant DuplicateSku with a field sku, and add_item(inv, item) that appends item to the end of the list. It raises DuplicateSku(sku) if an item with the same sku already exists.
Add at least one test for each new function.
sspur: fn remove_stock(inv: List[Item], sku: Str, n: Int where _ > 0) -> List[Item] ! fail[InvErr]; DuplicateSku{sku: Str} is a new variant of InvErr; fn add_item(inv: List[Item], item: Item) -> List[Item] ! fail[InvErr]
python: remove_stock(inv, sku, n) -> List[Item]; class DuplicateSku(InvErr) with attribute sku; add_item(inv, item) -> List[Item]

title: Word statistics: fix tie ordering, thread a new parameter through every function, add a function
steps: Bug: top_k must order by count descending and break ties by word ascending (alphabetically).

Add a stop-word parameter `stop` (a list of lowercase words) as the LAST parameter of words_of, word_freq, top_k, top_line and summary. Words in `stop` are excluded everywhere (after lowercasing), including the word count in summary. Update every caller and the existing tests (pass an empty list where no stop words are wanted).
Add longest_word(text): the longest word of words_of(text, []) (lowercased); ties go to the first occurrence; nothing if the text has no words.
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: fn words_of(text: Str, stop: List[Str]) -> List[Str]; fn word_freq(text: Str, stop: List[Str]) -> List[(Str, Int)]; fn top_k(text: Str, k: Int where _ >= 0, stop: List[Str]) -> List[(Str, Int)]; fn top_line(text: Str, k: Int where _ >= 0, stop: List[Str]) -> Str; fn summary(text: Str, stop: List[Str]) -> Str; fn longest_word(text: Str) -> Opt[Str]
python: words_of(text, stop); word_freq(text, stop); top_k(text, k, stop); top_line(text, k, stop); summary(text, stop); longest_word(text) -> Optional[str] (None when there are no words)

title: Bank: add a record field everywhere, a new error, a fee rule, and a new operation
steps: Add a field `frozen` (boolean) as the LAST field of Account. Every existing account and every account created by open_account starts unfrozen.
Add freeze(bank, id) that returns the bank with that account frozen. It raises UnknownAccount(id) if there is no such account.
Add an error variant Frozen with a field id. deposit and withdraw on a frozen account raise Frozen(id) (check this before the balance). So a transfer fails if the sender or the recipient is frozen.

Fee: a transfer of an amount below 50 costs the sender 1 extra (the sender loses amount + 1, the recipient gains amount, the fee goes nowhere). If the sender cannot cover amount + 1, raise Insufficient with needed = amount + 1.
attempt must report a frozen account as "declined: <id> is frozen".
Update the existing tests if needed and add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: type Account = {id: Str, owner: Str, balance: Int where _ >= 0, frozen: Bool}; fn freeze(bank: List[Account], id: Str) -> List[Account] ! fail[BankErr]; Frozen{id: Str} is a new variant of BankErr
python: Account(id, owner, balance, frozen) with frozen: bool as the 4th field; freeze(bank, id) -> List[Account]; class Frozen(BankErr) with attribute id

title: Expression calculator: add two variants and a new error through every function, add a query
steps: Add expression variants Sub (fields a, b) and Div (fields a, b). Evaluating Sub gives a - b; Div gives integer division a / b (tests only use non-negative operands). Division by zero raises a new error variant DivByZero (no fields) of CalcErr.
show: Sub prints as "(<a> - <b>)" and Div prints as "<a> / <b>" (like Mul, without parentheses).
simplify: also rewrite x - 0 to x and x / 1 to x (simplifying x), and otherwise simplify both children of Sub and Div.
run must report division by zero as "<show(e)> = error: division by zero".
Add var_names(e): the distinct variable names in e, in left-to-right order of first occurrence.
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: Sub{a: Expr, b: Expr} and Div{a: Expr, b: Expr} are new variants of Expr; DivByZero is a new variant of CalcErr; eval keeps its signature; fn var_names(e: Expr) -> List[Str]
python: @dataclass(frozen=True) classes Sub(a, b) and Div(a, b) added to Expr; class DivByZero(CalcErr) with no fields, raised by eval_expr; var_names(e) -> List[str]

title: Order pricing: rename a function across callers, add coupons, change dependent rules and output
steps: Rename subtotal to gross everywhere (the definition, every caller, and the tests).

Add discount(o) based on o.coupon: "SAVE10" gives 10% of gross; "BIG20" gives 20% of gross, but only when gross >= 10000 (otherwise 0); any other coupon (including "" and "FREESHIP") gives 0. Use integer division (round down).
Let net = gross - discount. Tax becomes 8% of net (integer division). Shipping becomes 0 when net >= 5000 or the coupon is "FREESHIP", otherwise 499. Total becomes net + shipping + tax.
invoice becomes "order <id>: gross <g>, discount <d>, shipping <s>, tax <t>, total <T>", with every amount formatted by money.
Update the existing tests and add tests for the coupons.
sspur: fn gross(o: Order) -> Int; fn discount(o: Order) -> Int; shipping, tax, total, invoice keep their signatures
python: gross(o) -> int; discount(o) -> int; shipping, tax, total, invoice keep their signatures

title: Todo list: introduce errors into an existing function and its callers, add rendering and three functions
steps: Add an error type TaskErr with variants NotFound (field id) and AlreadyDone (field id). complete(ts, id) raises NotFound(id) if no task has that id, and AlreadyDone(id) if the task is already done. Update its callers (main, tests) accordingly.
render includes the priority label in parentheses: "[ ] #2 (high) write report". Labels are low, med, high.
Add by_priority(ts): the pending tasks only, High first, then Med, then Low; equal priorities in ascending id order.
Add clear_done(ts): removes every done task, keeping order.
Add retitle(ts, id, title): changes that task's title; raises NotFound(id) if missing.
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: type TaskErr = NotFound{id: Int} | AlreadyDone{id: Int}; fn complete(ts: List[Task], id: Int) -> List[Task] ! fail[TaskErr]; fn by_priority(ts: List[Task]) -> List[Task]; fn clear_done(ts: List[Task]) -> List[Task]; fn retitle(ts: List[Task], id: Int, title: Str) -> List[Task] ! fail[TaskErr]
python: class TaskErr(Exception); class NotFound(TaskErr) and class AlreadyDone(TaskErr), each with attribute id; complete(ts, id); by_priority(ts); clear_done(ts); retitle(ts, id, title)

title: Grade book: fix two bugs and a tie rule, add three functions
steps: Bug: average of a student with no scores must be 0 (it currently crashes).
Bug: letter thresholds are inclusive: 90 and above is A, 80 and above B, 70 and above C, 60 and above D, otherwise F.
ranking: break ties in average by name ascending.
Add drop_lowest(s): if the student has at least 2 scores, remove exactly one occurrence of the lowest score (the rest keep their order); otherwise return the student unchanged.
Add curve(ss, pts), pts >= 0: add pts to every score of every student, capping each score at 100.
Add honor_roll(ss): the names of students whose grade is A after drop_lowest, sorted by name.
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: fn drop_lowest(s: Student) -> Student; fn curve(ss: List[Student], pts: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Student]; fn honor_roll(ss: List[Student]) -> List[Str]
python: drop_lowest(s) -> Student; curve(ss, pts) -> List[Student]; honor_roll(ss) -> List[str]

title: Config parser: harden parsing in four ways, add typed getters with new error variants
steps: Trim whitespace around each entry, key, and value. Skip entries with no "=", and entries whose key is empty after trimming.
Split each entry at the FIRST "=" only: "url=a=b" has key url and value "a=b".
Entries whose trimmed text starts with "#" are comments and are skipped.
lookup returns the value of the LAST entry with that key (later entries override earlier ones). keys still lists distinct keys in first-seen order.
Add get_int(cfg, key): raises Missing(key) if absent, and a new variant NotInt(key, value) if the value is not an integer (an optional leading "-" followed by digits).

Add get_bool(cfg, key, default): "true", "yes", "1" give true and "false", "no", "0" give false (case-insensitive); a missing key gives default; any other value raises a new variant NotBool(key, value).
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: NotInt{key: Str, value: Str} and NotBool{key: Str, value: Str} are new variants of CfgErr; fn get_int(cfg: List[Entry], key: Str) -> Int ! fail[CfgErr]; fn get_bool(cfg: List[Entry], key: Str, default: Bool) -> Bool ! fail[CfgErr]
python: class NotInt(CfgErr) and class NotBool(CfgErr), each with attributes key and value; get_int(cfg, key) -> int; get_bool(cfg, key, default) -> bool

title: Event log: switch the parser to a regex, add JSON export and import, redaction, and skipped lines
steps: parse_line must accept only the new format "[<ts>] <LEVEL>: <msg>": ts is one or more digits, LEVEL is one or more uppercase letters A-Z, msg is the rest of the line with surrounding whitespace trimmed (it may be empty). Use a regular expression. The old "|" format and anything else give nothing. Update sample and the tests.
Add to_json(evs): compact JSON (no spaces) of the list, each event an object with fields ts, level, msg in that order, for example [{"ts":1,"level":"INFO","msg":"up"}].

Add an error type EventErr with a variant BadJson (field text), and from_json(s): the events in a JSON array of such objects. Raise BadJson(s) if s is not valid JSON or does not have that shape (ts an integer, level and msg strings, none missing).

Add redact(e): the event with every email address in msg replaced by "<email>". An email is one or more of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, then @, then one or more of A-Z a-z 0-9 -, then one or more groups of a dot followed by one or more of A-Z a-z 0-9 -.
Add skipped(lines): the lines that ingest skips, in order.
Add tests for the new behavior.
sspur: fn parse_line(line: Str) -> Opt[Event]; type EventErr = BadJson{text: Str}; fn to_json(evs: List[Event]) -> Str; fn from_json(s: Str) -> List[Event] ! fail[EventErr]; fn redact(e: Event) -> Event; fn skipped(lines: List[Str]) -> List[Str]
python: parse_line(line) -> Optional[Event]; class EventErr(Exception); class BadJson(EventErr) with attribute text; to_json(evs) -> str; from_json(s) -> List[Event]; redact(e) -> Event; skipped(lines) -> List[str]
